s: Socket.IO, SSE, WebSocket protocol, real-time patterns
d: HTTP is request-response. WebSockets enable persistent, bidirectional communication — essential for chat, live notifications, real-time dashboards, collaborative editing, and gaming. Server-Sent Events (SSE) is simpler for server-to-client streaming.

p: WebSockets provide full-duplex, persistent, bidirectional communication over a single TCP connection. Unlike HTTP (request-response), WebSockets allow the server to push data to the client instantly.
1. Client sends HTTP request with 'Upgrade: websocket' header.
2. Server agrees, connection is upgraded to WebSocket.
3. Both client and server can send/receive messages freely.
4. Used for Chat apps, Live tracking, Multiplayer games.

// Socket.io Example (Server)
io.on('connection', (socket) => {
  console.log('User connected');
  socket.on('chat_msg', (msg) => {
    io.emit('chat_msg', msg); // Broadcast to everyone
  });
});

HTTP (Polling):                   WebSocket:
Client -> "Any news?" -> Server   Client <======> Server
Client <- "No"        <-          (Persistent Connection)
Client -> "Any news?" -> Server   Server -> "New msg!" -> Client
Client <- "Yes!"      <-          Server -> "Typing..." -> Client
